title: Inference metrics TTL and drift-detection pipeline
creator: Evan Liu
description: Introduce a pipeline stage and retention/TTL policy for inference KPIs that detects distribution drift and automatically tiers (hot/warm/cold) time-series. Goals: reduce storage costs for high-cardinality inference metrics, surface regressions quickly via drift alerts, and preserve sufficient resolution for root-cause debugging. The work touches the OTLP ingestion layer, Prometheus adapter, KPI enrichment stage, and downstream dashboards/alerts. This ticket covers schema additions, collector processors, drift scoring, TTL enforcement, migration of existing series to tiered storage, and dashboard/alert updates.
background: Recent burst in model variant and routing labels increased high-cardinality series and storage costs. Teams reported slower ad-hoc investigations because some debug metrics were downsampled aggressively. We need a mechanism to (1) automatically identify stable vs. drifting KPI series, (2) keep full-resolution hot data for drifting/important series, and (3) apply TTL/rollup for stable/cold series to reduce cost while keeping SLO-aligned fidelity.
approach: 1) Add 'kpi_tier' label produced by a new collector processor: hot | warm | cold. 2) Implement a drift-scoring service that consumes aggregated windows (1m/5m) and marks series with sustained distribution change. 3) Integrate TTL enforcement in the Prometheus write path and the metrics-fanout router to route cold series to long-term storage with rollups. 4) Provide a reversible promotion path when a cold series begins to drift. 5) Add Grafana dashboards and alert rules (drift score, tier churn, storage delta).
tradeoffs: Keeping too many series hot increases cost; being too aggressive risks losing debug fidelity for regressions. We will start conservative (longer warm period) and iterate based on observed false-negative drift misses. Drift scoring introduces near-real-time compute; we will batch-window and backpressure via the enrichment layer to avoid amplifying ingestion costs.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged rollout in collector in staging. 2) Shadow drift scoring for 2 weeks (no tier changes). 3) Enable promotion/demotion for non-critical namespaces (internal, staging). 4) Ramp to production namespaces with SLA guardrails. 5) Run a migration job to tag existing series and apply TTL rules in phases.
acceptance_criteria: Drift scoring service emits drift_score for 95% of active series with <5s processing latency for 1m windows.
kpi_tier label applied consistently and visible in Prometheus ingestion for test namespaces.
Cold-series rollup reduces storage usage for high-cardinality cohort by >=40% in 30 days in staged environment.
Dashboards show tier distribution and drift churn; alert fires when drift_score exceeds threshold for a model route.
Promotion path works end-to-end: a cold series can be promoted to hot within 5 minutes and full-resolution data retained thereafter.
risks: Drift algorithms may create oscillation churn between tiers if thresholds are not tuned. Prometheus adapter must handle label cardinality changes gracefully to avoid series explosion. Rollback plan must ensure we can rehydrate recent samples for investigations.
migration_notes: We will run a background job that samples recent series, scores them, and assigns an initial kpi_tier. For historical retention, a one-time rollup job will compute 1m->5m aggregates for cold candidates older than 7 days before applying TTL. Migration PR: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/1423.
dashboards_and_alerts: Grafana: 'Inference KPI Tiering Overview' dashboard (panel: tier heatmap by model/route, drift trend, storage delta). Alerts: inference.kpi.drift_high -> Pager; inference.kpi.tier_churn_high -> #telemetry-alerts Slack. Dashboard draft: grafana.redwood.internal/d/inf-kpi-tiering/overview (draft).
implementation_notes: Collector changes in otel-collector config: add processor 'kpi_tierer' and exporter tag to pass 'kpi_tier' to prometheus adapter. Drift service implemented as a lightweight Flink job (or k8s microservice) reading aggregated windows from Kafka topic 'kpi-agg-1m'. Prometheus adapter must expose a TTL label that write-path uses to place series into tiered storage buckets.
security_considerations: No new customer PII flows. Ensure drift service runs with least privilege to Kafka and storage. Audit logs must tag any automated promotions/demotions for compliance.
testing_plan: Unit tests for drift scoring edge cases, integration tests in staging with synthetic workload that simulates variant explosions, e2e test for promotion/demotion path and TTL enforcement. Load test: simulate 2x current ingestion spike and validate backpressure handling.
